segments.script: Every blink, every breath, every heartbeat — powered by muscle. Three types, three jobs, one molecular secret.
segments.video_prompt: Triptych animation. Left: striated skeletal muscle fibres contract in parallel — striations visible with the I-band narrowing. Centre: a smooth muscle ring contracts around a gut tube, pushing a bolus forward. Right: cardiac muscle network pulsates in branching waves with an ECG waveform running below. Each panel is colour-coded: blue for skeletal, green for smooth, red for cardiac. Cinematic molecular biology style.

segments.script: Muscular tissue is mesodermal. Actin and myosin slide in the sliding filament theory of Huxley and Hanson. Skeletal (striped) muscle: multi-nucleated, unbranched, cylindrical. Sarcomere bands: A-band, I-band, H-band, M-line, Z-lines. During contraction: I-band narrows, H-band disappears, A-band unchanged. Red muscle has myoglobin and is fatigue-resistant. White muscle lacks myoglobin and is fast-twitch. Voluntary; fatigues quickly. Smooth (unstriped) muscle: uninucleated, spindle-shaped, no visible striations. Single-unit contracts as one (bladder, gut). Multi-unit contracts independently (blood vessels, arrector pilli). Involuntary, fatigues in 10–12 hours, performs peristalsis. Cardiac muscle: branched, connected by intercalated discs (desmosomes plus gap junctions) — functional syncytium. Never fatigues. Only in the heart. Least abundant. Total muscles 639: largest gluteus maximus, smallest stapedius, longest sartorius, strongest masseter.
segments.video_prompt: Sequence: (1) Sarcomere animation — resting state all bands labelled, then contraction — I-band collapses, H-band vanishes, Z-lines approach. (2) Peristalsis animation — gut tube cross section, muscle rings contract in a wave pushing the bolus leftward. (3) Intercalated disc close-up — step-shaped junction with desmosomes labelled at lateral sides and gap junctions at transverse portions, shown as molecular structures. (4) Fun facts ticker: 639 muscles, gluteus maximus, stapedius, sartorius, masseter. Clean molecular illustration, blue-gold palette.
